title: Drupal fixes critical core flaw that can let attackers reinstall a site and run code (CVE-2026-132165)
summary: Drupal rated SA-CORE-2026-017, CVE-2026-132165, critical: under specific conditions install.php can be used to reinstall a site, leading to takeover or code execution. Drupal says a proof of concept exists. Fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13. A second advisory, CVE-2026-132166, is a gadget chain that is not directly exploitable. Drupal credits Anthropic's OSS Scanner for finding the first.
plain: Drupal fixed a serious flaw that could let an attacker take over a website by re-running its installer. Example attack code exists.
exec: Drupal runs a large number of public websites; a critical flaw with a proof of concept needs a quick update.
action: Update Drupal core to 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13 (or later). If you cannot upgrade, secure the installer as Drupal describes. Sites on 11.2.x and 10.5.x or older are end of life.

key_findings: SA-CORE-2026-017 (Critical, CVE-2026-132165): installer reinstall leading to takeover or RCE; proof of concept exists.
SA-CORE-2026-018 (CVE-2026-132166) is a gadget chain needing a separate unsafe-unserialize flaw.
recommendations: Upgrade; secure the installer if you cannot.

validation.note: Read both Drupal security advisories (primary); NCSC-NL also lists the release.
